resources.string: Connect Gmail and GitHub accounts; review local mail drafts

Credentials and local drafts are encrypted with the device Keystore, excluded from backups, and never given to the model. Read tools expose selected external content to the configured model. Treat mail and repository text as untrusted data. Enable the Gmail / GitHub tool groups in the assistant settings. External writes always require a fresh approval of one exact call, even in Auto mode. Background tasks may read and prepare local drafts, but cannot send, upload drafts, or post to GitHub.

Requires Google Play services. Signing in to Google does not grant Gmail access. App maintainers configure Google Cloud once; ordinary users only select an account and grant access. Open the step-by-step guide if connection fails.

Each capability requests its own permission on demand. Google gmail.compose also permits sending, but CLmA still requires the separate send switch and per-call approval. Turning a switch off blocks that capability locally; disconnect with revoke to remove Google grants.

Use a GitHub App with Device Flow enabled. Configure only the repositories and repository permissions you need: Metadata / Issues / Pull requests read access; Issues write access only if posting is needed. Install the App on selected repositories first. Enter its public Client ID, never a client secret or token. User tokens may expire; reconnect when required.
Enter this code at the official GitHub device authorization page. CLmA waits here; leaving this page cancels polling. Do not share the code.

Saving here does not upload or send mail. Ask the assistant to read the latest draft and request a new approval with the complete account, recipients, subject and body. A changed draft invalidates an old preview. For sending/uploading/unknown states, check Gmail before taking further action; CLmA never retries automatically.

Disconnecting deletes the local account reference and all encrypted local Gmail drafts. Sent mail and remote drafts are not deleted. Reconnect to restore access; deleted local drafts cannot be recovered.
Removes the local user token. Reconnect to restore access. This does not uninstall the GitHub App or revoke it remotely; manage remote access in GitHub Settings > Applications.

Review the complete account, target, recipients/title and body. This approval authorizes exactly one external write. Chat-wide grants, Auto mode, direct execution and unattended tasks cannot approve it. If the outcome is uncertain, check the remote service before requesting another write.
Delete local draft “%1$s”? This cannot be undone. Uploaded Gmail drafts and sent mail are not removed.
Operation failed: %1$s. Check authorization, account configuration and network access.
Google authorization was cancelled (status 16). Signing in to Google alone does not grant Gmail access.

Google OAuth configuration error (status 10). The developer must register an Android OAuth client for this package and signing certificate, enable Gmail API, and configure the consent screen and test users.
Google authorization could not reach Google services (status 7). Check the connectivity available to Google Play services; the in-app proxy does not configure Play services.
Google authorization returned no result. This does not establish that you cancelled. Check Google Play services and the Android OAuth configuration.

Who needs to configure this? Ordinary users do not need a Google Cloud project. The app maintainer or a developer distributing their own build configures OAuth. If that setup is missing or your account is not an allowed test user, signing in repeatedly cannot fix it; contact the maintainer.
For ordinary users: connect and grant Gmail access

Make sure Google Play services can reach Google. Return to Gmail, tap Connect and grant read access, choose the account, and approve Gmail reading. Connection is complete only when your email address appears. If authorization is denied, ask the maintainer to check the configuration below; do not create a separate project just to use the official app.
Developer step 1: create or select one project

Open Google Cloud Console and use the project selector at the top. Create a project such as CLmA or select an existing one. Keep the same project selected for every step below. These buttons open official Google pages; they do not submit configuration for you.
Open the Gmail API page in the selected project and choose Enable. If the API is already enabled, leave it enabled. An API key by itself cannot authorize access to Gmail.

Open Google Auth Platform → Branding and choose Get started if prompted. Enter the app name, support email, and developer contact details. Complete the required branding fields with accurate information; production use may require a homepage and privacy policy.
Step 4: set the audience and test users

Open Audience. For personal Gmail accounts, use an External audience. While the app is in Testing, add the exact Google account that will authorize CLmA under Test users and save. Signing into the device does not add an account to this list.
Step 5: add the Gmail read scope

Open Data Access, choose Add or remove scopes, and add the read-only scope below. Save the change. Start with read access; CLmA requests sending and remote-draft access separately when you enable those features.

Open Clients → Create client and select Android, not Web application. Copy the package name and signing certificate SHA-1 shown below into the corresponding fields, then create the client. These values are read from this installed app, so debug or re-signed builds will differ. No Client ID, client secret, or JSON file needs to be pasted into CLmA for this flow.
The installed signing certificate could not be read. Do not guess a fingerprint; obtain the certificate SHA-1 from the build maintainer.
Step 7: return to CLmA and try connecting

Save the Cloud changes, return to CLmA, and connect again. Configuration changes may take time to propagate. Status 10 means a developer configuration error; 7 means a Google services network error; 16 means cancellation. A missing result is not proof of cancellation. Send the exact status to the maintainer; do not send mail or tokens. The in-app proxy does not configure Google Play services traffic.

Testing is not a public rollout. Gmail scopes can require Google verification and a security assessment before production use. A tutorial or a passing build does not complete that review or prove live authorization works.

Never share a Google password, access token, refresh token, client secret, signing keystore, or service-account key. The package name and certificate fingerprint are public identifiers. Keep external writes on per-call approval.
Read the official Android authorization guide
